items.title: 1.3 Uncertainty (ghair yaqeeni, pakka na hona) in measurement (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Kitab ke pages to aap bilkul theek gin sakte hain, magar kitab ki length napne ke liye koi napne wala instrument chahiye. Har instrument par sab se chhote division tak nishan lage hote hain (isay calibration kehte hain), aur yahi baat us ki accuracy (kitna sahi) ki limit tay karti hai. Kisi instrument se reading lein to us ki measurement ki limit us ke scale ka sab se chhota division hoti hai. Is liye har napi gayi quantity mein kuch na kuch uncertainty (pakka na hona) hoti hai. Measurement scale ke sab se qareebi nishan tak li jati hai. Zyada se zyada uncertainty ko instrument ke ek sab se chhote division ke barabar maana ja sakta hai; ise absolute uncertainty kehte hain. Millimetre wale metre rule par yeh ek millimetre hai. Example: agar kitab ka ek edge (kinara) 10.0 cm ke nishan par aur doosra 33.5 cm par ho, to length uncertainty ke saath yeh hai:

Iska matlab hai ke kitab ki asal (true) length 23.4 cm aur 23.6 cm ke darmiyan hai. Har end (sire) par uncertainty ±0.05 cm hai; dono milkar length mein 0.1 cm ki uncertainty banti hai, jo metre rule ke least count ke barabar hai. Uncertainty in tareeqon se likhi ja sakti hai:

blocks.text_alt: Fractional uncertainty = Absolute uncertainty / Measured value
ya Percentage uncertainty = (Absolute uncertainty / Measured value) × 100

blocks.text: Kitab pehle kehti hai ke zyada se zyada uncertainty ek poora chhota division (1 mm) hai, phir misal mein har reading par aadha division (±0.05 cm) leti hai. Dono readings ki ±0.05 cm add ho kar ±0.1 cm, yani ek poora least count, ban jati hai. Exam mein aam taur par ek reading ki absolute uncertainty = least count li jati hai.
